yaml.title: Research
yaml.subtitle: How we measure political beliefs, and what those measurements can tell us

markdown.markdown:
My research brings together political theory, data science and statistical methods, with interests spanning computational international relations, political theory, predictive modelling and machine learning. Right now I'm part of the [Data Impact Lab](https://data-impact.pages.dev/). ::: {.timeline} ::: {.project data-when="Jun 2026 – Present"} [Lead Author, Data Impact Lab]{.role} ### Psychometric Measurement in Large Language Models [Supervised by Dr Jie Kang and Dr Kangning Du]{.people} ::: {.questions} - Can an AI change its mind? - Ask it the same question twice and the answer can shift. Why? - Ask in another language. Does the answer change? - Does it take sides? And if it leans left or right, is it good at hiding it? ::: I study these questions by giving large language models the same political psychology scales used with people, and testing whether the measurements hold up: what it means for a model to "hold" an attitude, and how far tools built for people can be trusted when they are applied to AI. ::: {.outputs} - *Accepted* Abstract, 12th Charles Perkins Centre EMCR Symposium - *Submitted* Manuscript, collection "Large Language Models in Psychological Science", *Humanities and Social Sciences Communications* (Nature Portfolio) ::: ::: ::: {.project data-when="Sep 2026 – Present"} [Student Researcher, recipient 2026]{.role} ### Sydney Policy Reform Project [Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, University of Sydney]{.people} - Co-authoring a policy paper for ANTAR, *Civics Education and Truth-Readiness: An International Comparative Analysis*. - Contributing research to policy and law reform for community organisations and public agencies. ::: ::: {.project data-when="Jul – Sep 2026"} [Statistical Analyst and Contributing Author, Data Impact Lab]{.role} ### Facial Expression Studies [With Professor Ted Ruffman, University of Otago]{.people} Finished the statistical analysis for two manuscripts. ::: {.outputs} - *In preparation* *Journal of Nonverbal Behavior* (Springer Nature) - *In preparation* *Cognition and Emotion* (Taylor & Francis Group) ::: ::: ::: {.project data-when="2025"} [Summer Research Scholar, Charles Perkins Centre]{.role} ### Statistical Modelling for Policy-Making [Supervised by A/Prof Clara Grazian (Mathematics & Statistics) and Prof Alexandre Lefebvre (Politics & Philosophy)]{.people} - Built an OLS predictive model to support policy-making. - Provided the theoretical framework, drawing on Samuel Moyn's critique of human rights and Elizabeth Anderson's *Private Government*. ::: ::: ## Data visualisation ```{=html}
